piece.title: Dorian Drift

motif.name: long_arc
motif.notes: Twice the length of the last two motifs on purpose -- 12 notes over a full 2-bar (8-beat) cycle instead of 1-bar/4-beat, so the line has room to breathe and arc rather than repeat every bar. Mostly stepwise with one small leap (the 3), gentle rise-and-fall shape closer to a sung phrase than a riff. 'augmentation' in the transform pool lets it stretch out even further on repetition.

piece.notes: Chill modal jazz: Tyner-style dorian vamping (i-IV-VII movement, the same harmonic neighborhood as 'My Favorite Things') with Evans-style lush open voicings and a pedal bass instead of a walking line. Every major chord (III/IV/VII, all diatonic to dorian -- no borrowed accidentals needed, so plain roman numerals without a 'b' prefix) carries a 9 or add13 for color; i stays minor9 throughout as the harmonic anchor. voicing='open' spreads everything for that airy Evans spacing; harmony_rhythm='sustain' holds pads instead of comping stabs -- opposite mood from the funk piece. No drums -- this is a piano-trio-chill vibe, not a groove track. Honest limitation: this engine doesn't have a literal quartal-voicing mode (stacked fourths as a distinct chord-building method) -- Tyner's exact sound is approximated here through mode + tensions + open spacing + a slow pedal-point bass, not a true quartal harmony feature.

main_vamp.notes: The vamp -- i minor9 as home base, IV and VII (both diatonic major chords in dorian, no accidentals) drifting through and back. Long pedal bass underneath, no walking motion.

bridge.notes: Brief lift into dorian's relative-major color (III) before settling back through IV-VII into home.
